Maintenance Report — MNT-0040-004

Asset: WELL-0040 (SW-23 Well 040, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: flowline Work started: 28 Apr 2023 08:00 · Finished: 29 Apr 2023 05:00 · Well stopped for this job: 21 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Daniel Foster Triggered by: inspection INS-0040-0028 on 2023-04-27 Report written: 29 Apr 2023

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0040-0028 at 10:15 on 2023-04-27 found crude oil on the pad: about 4.5% of the pad area, estimated 2.4 bbl. The inspector noted: "Pooled fluid near flowline." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 5.5 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Corrosion under a failed protective wrap on the coupling.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 245 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 196 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 1.6 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0040-004 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.74% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0040-013

Asset: WELL-0040 (SW-23 Well 040, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: flowline Work started: 12 May 2024 08:00 · Finished: 15 May 2024 15:00 · Well stopped for this job: 79 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Megan Ward · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0040-0079 on 2024-05-09 Report written: 16 May 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the inspector saw wet soil above the buried flowline. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0040-0079 showed the wellhead at 26.6 °C with the air at 26.0 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line. The well stayed shut in for about 1 day longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

Root cause

Internal corrosion from produced water collecting at a low point.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 2% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joint.
  5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: cut out and replaced the corroded flowline section.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 245 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 196 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Oily soil from the excavation and the cut-out pipe sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0040-013 (WS-06).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0040-024

Asset: WELL-0040 (SW-23 Well 040, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: wellhead Work started: 14 Mar 2026 08:00 · Finished: 17 Mar 2026 01:00 · Well stopped for this job: 65 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Brian Coleman · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0040-0174 on 2026-03-12 Report written: 18 Mar 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that fluid was weeping from the stuffing box around the polished rod. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0040-0174 showed the wellhead at 18.9 °C with the air at 13.6 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The packing rings were worn and the polished rod was lightly scored.

Root cause

Normal packing wear.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 3 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Closed the wellhead valves and bled off pressure.
  2. Removed the old packing.
  3. Installed new packing rings and adjusted the gland.
  4. Cleaned the wellhead area.

Summary of the fix: replaced stuffing box packing.

Testing and return to service

Checked the stuffing box with the unit running: no leak. The well was returned to production.
